en: Oṃ, homage to all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas!
Thus have I heard: at one time the Blessed One was dwelling in Śrāvastī, in the Karīṭa Grove.
And in the Karī-maṇḍala:
Then indeed the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, surrounded by many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of vidyādharas, approached the place where the Blessed One was.
Having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One, circumambulated the Blessed One, and—
Having performed his duties, he sat down beside the Blessed One and addressed him as follows:
"O Blessed One, this heart-mantra of mine named *Ekādaśamukha* was spoken by eleven *koṭis* of Buddhas.
And now, at this time..."
If so, then I shall speak for the sake, welfare, and happiness of all sentient beings; for the pacification of all diseases;

for the warding off of all evil, misfortune, and bad dreams; for the warding off of all untimely death; for the inspiration of those who lack faith; and for the pacification of all obstacles and impediments.
"O Blessed One, I do not perceive anything in this world with its gods, Māras, and Brahmās, among this generation with its ascetics and brahmins,

that can [counteract] when this heart has been made into a protection, a defense, a refuge, a source of peace and well-being, an avoidance of punishment, an avoidance of weapons, and a neutralizer of poison."
Once the poison has been eliminated, it is impossible that there should be no further pacification of whatever transgression remains;
setting aside past karma, for one who is thus reflecting and placing full faith, all of that will cease to exist in every respect.
This heart-mantra is praised by all Buddhas and is attended to by them; this heart-mantra is rejoiced in by all Tathāgatas.

O Blessed One, I remember that more than a hundred eons ago, as many as the sands of the river Gaṅgā, [there was a time] when... [the one named] Śatapadmanayanacūḍāpratihatasaṅgavelāma... [was present].

"O King, this was heard by me in the presence of the Tathāgata Raṅgavelakiraṇa. 1.10 "This was heard by me in the presence of the Tathāgata... [The text continues: "...anuśrutenāyaṃ. [Note: The manuscript reading *rājā* is supported by the codex, while Dutt emends it to *rājasya*. The phrase *anuśrutenāyaṃ* is supplied by Ken.]
Upon hearing this, it was grasped in the heart.

Simultaneously with its acquisition, all the Tathāgatas in the ten directions became well-disposed toward him, and he attained the patient acceptance of the non-arising of phenomena (anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti).
Thus, this *Hṛdaya* is of great benefit. Therefore, a faithful son of good family or daughter of good family should, with reverence, accomplish this *Hṛdaya*;
it should be accomplished constantly with an undistracted mind. [It should be recited] at dawn...
Having risen at dawn, one should recite it one hundred and eight times.
Ten qualities pertaining to the present life are to be acquired.
Which ten?
[1] Namely, he will be free from disease;
[2] and he will be embraced by all.
[3] His accumulation of wealth, grain, and gold shall become inexhaustible.
[4] All enemies shall be brought under his control and subdued.
[5] In the royal assembly...
In the assembly, he will first think that he must address [the matter];
neither poison, nor cumulative toxins, nor fever, nor weapons shall take effect upon his body.
[7] He shall not die by water. [8] He shall not die by fire. [9] He shall not die by untimely death.
And he will bring about his time [of death].
Furthermore, there are four other qualities and benefits that one who takes up [this teaching] will obtain:
[1] at the time of death, there will be a vision of the Tathāgata;
[2] one will not be reborn in the miserable realms.
[3] He shall not die an untimely death due to an uneven [mortality].
[4] Having passed away from here, he will be reborn in the world-system Sukhāvatī.
"O Blessed One, I remember that ten eons ago, as numerous as the sands of ten Ganges rivers, and even further back than that, there was a Tathāgata named Mandāravagandha."
There, while I was being treated with contempt by householders, I took up this [teaching].
For forty thousand kalpas, the cycles of saṃsāra were turned back. And having set it forth in my heart, [I have proclaimed] this for all the Buddhas.
He attained the bodhisattva liberation called the "Womb of Knowledge that Compassionates All," by means of which—

By this [merit], may I become a shelter, a protection, a refuge, and a final resort for all sentient beings— those who are bound by fetters, those who have reached the point of execution, and those afflicted by the various sufferings of water and fire.

Having drawn in all the wicked yakṣas and rākṣasas by means of this heart-mantra, and having made them possess minds of loving-kindness and compassion, I establish them in unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
Thus, O Blessed One, by revealing this heart-mantra of mine, which possesses such great purpose, even once, the four root transgressions go to destruction.
They will diminish the five deeds of immediate retribution without remainder;
what need is there to mention those who will practice according to what has been taught?
"What need is there to say more?
These things will come to pass exactly as they have been taught."
Those who hear [this] will have planted roots of merit under many hundreds of thousands of Buddhas, let alone through recitation, ritual accomplishment (*sādhana*),
and so forth.
I shall fulfill all desires.
And those [who observe] the fourteenth and fifteenth [days]...
Dutt: "It should be 'on the fourteenth or the fifteenth'. Those who observe the fast for my sake will turn their backs on the cycle of existence (*saṃsāra*) for forty thousand *kalpas*.

By the mere grasping of that name, O Blessed One, this is equal to more than hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Buddhas. By the grasping of my name, all sentient beings attain the state of non-retrogression and are completely liberated from all diseases.
They shall be completely liberated from all obscurations, from all fears, and from all misconduct of body, speech, and mind; for them,
the awakening of a Buddha will be as if held in the palm of their hand.
The Blessed One said:
"Excellent, excellent, son of good family, that you [should do so]!"
Since you possess such great compassion toward all sentient beings,
will you be able, O son of good family?
Noble son, by this means I have taken up and rejoiced in this heart-mantra (*hṛdaya*) in order to establish all sentient beings in unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
"Speak, son of good family!
Then, indeed, the noble Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara rose up.
Rising from his seat, having arranged his upper robe over one shoulder and prostrating at the feet of the Blessed One, he recited this heart-mantra:
Homage to the Three Jewels!
Homage to the Tathāgata Vairocana!
Homage to the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, the Greatly Compassionate One!
Homage to all the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Perfectly Awakened Ones of the past, future, and present. Oṃ diri diri.
dhara dhara dhiri dhiri / dhuru dhuru / iṭṭe viṭṭe /
Cale cale / pracale pracale / kusume kusumavare /
*ili mili ciṭi svāhā*.
Thus is the root mantra.
Homage to the Three Jewels!
Homage to the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara!
It is thus: *ha ha ha ha*.
Hā [hā hā] hā!
Hime tile cile bhile khile svāhā!
[For] bathing and ritual sipping.
By touching [the garment], sprinkling it with water, and reciting the mantra seven times:
"Homage to the Three Jewels."
Homage to the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara.
It is as follows: *ṭuru ṭuru ha ha ha ha svāhā*.
The mantra for the offering of incense and lamps:
Homage to the Three Jewels!
Homage to the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara!
Namely: *siri siri dhiri dhiri siri dhiri svāhā*.
This is the mantra for the offering of perfumes and flowers.
Homage to the Three Jewels!
Homage to the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, the Greatly Compassionate One!
It is thus: sāde sāde!
*sidi sidi / sudu sudu svāhā*. By reciting this mantra for the offering of the *bali* twenty-one times.
Homage to the Triple Gem!
Homage to the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara,
the Greatly Compassionate One!
Namely: *masi ddhasi cari huru icuruḥ suruḥ suru svāhā*.
Regarding the *homa* mantras:

having kindled a fire with *jātī* wood using this mantra, one should perform thirty *homa* offerings of [fuel sticks] smeared with curd, honey, and ghee, by means of a single person who has fasted for a day and night.
Then one should begin the ritual action:
Homage to the Three Jewels!
Homage to the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, the Great Compassionate One.
It is thus: ili mili pili tili.
*Tili hili svāhā*.
The binding of the directions (*diśābandha*) is performed with water, or with mustard seeds, or with ashes, by reciting [the mantra] seven times.
Homage to the Three Jewels! Homage to the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara,
the Greatly Compassionate One!
Namely: piṭi piṭi, tiṭi tiṭi,
viṭi viṭi, go, go, Bhagavan!
Bhagavān Āryāvalokiteśvara, svabhavanaṃ svabhavanaṃ svāhā!
Having recited this seven times over water, one should scatter it in the four directions.
The reading of the manuscripts should mean that the *sādhaka* speaks these words as part of the mantra:
"Noble Avalokiteśvara, go to your own abode!"
At the end of the *Hayagrīvāvidyā*, a different hand has added:
*Oṃ namo ratnatrayāya; namaś caṇḍavajrapāṇaye mahāśaktisenāpataye. Tadyathā: ugrāya svāhā.*
To the exceedingly fierce one, svāhā!
To the one dear to Ugra, svāhā! To the one dear to Ugra, svāhā!
(derived from *rudrapriya* and similar terms).
